arxiv-2103-04260.title: ARVo: Learning All-Range Volumetric Correspondence for Video Deblurring
arxiv-2103-04260.creator: Dongxu Li, Chenchen Xu, Kaihao Zhang, Xin Yu, Yiran Zhong, Wenqi Ren, Hanna Suominen, Hongdong Li
arxiv-2103-04260.description: Abstract † † footnotetext: ∗ * Authors contributed equally. † \dagger Corresponding author: kaihao.zhang@anu.edu.au . Video deblurring models exploit consecutive frames to remove blurs from camera shakes and object motions. In order to utilize neighboring sharp patches, typical methods rely mainly on homography or optical flows to spatially align neighboring blurry frames.

arxiv-2109-08680.title: The influence of an external magnetic field on cold plasma oscillations
arxiv-2109-08680.creator: Olga S. Rozanova*, Eugeniy V. Chizhonkov
arxiv-2109-08680.description: Abstract . For a system of equations describing one-dimensional nonlinear oscillations in a magnetoactive plasma, we study the effect of a constant magnetic field on the breaking of oscillations. For the nonrelativistic case, a criterion for the formation of a finite-dimensional singularity is obtained in terms of the initial data.

arxiv-2109-09423.title: Photoinjector Generation of High-Charge Magnetized Beams for Electron-Cooling Applications
arxiv-2109-09423.creator: A. Fetterman, D. Mihalcea, S. Benson, D. Crawford, D. Edstrom, F. Hannon, P. Piot, J. Ruan, S. Wang
arxiv-2109-09423.description: Abstract Electron-cooling offers a relatively simple scheme to enable high-luminosity collisions in future electron-ion and hadron colliders. Contemplated TeV-energy hadron colliders require relativistic (sub 100 MeV) high-charge [ 𝒪 ⁡ ( nC ) {\cal O}(\mbox{nC}) ] electron beams with a specific transverse eigenemittance partition. This paper discusses the generation of high-charge ( Q ≤ 3.2 Q\leq 3.

arxiv-2111-15182.title: Easy Semantification of Bioassays Thanks: Supported by TIB Leibniz Information Centre for Science and Technology, the EU H2020 ERC project ScienceGRaph (GA ID: 819536) and the ITN PERICO (GA ID: 812968).
arxiv-2111-15182.creator: Marco Anteghini, Jennifer D’Souza, Vitor A.P. Martins dos Santos, Sören Auer
arxiv-2111-15182.description: Abstract Biological data and knowledge bases increasingly rely on Semantic Web technologies and the use of knowledge graphs for data integration, retrieval and federated queries. We propose a solution for automatically semantifying biological assays . Our solution contrasts the problem of automated semantification as labeling versus clustering where the two methods are on opposite ends of the method complexity spectrum.

arxiv-2209-14220.title: New Constraints on Warm Dark Matter from the Lyman- α \alpha Forest Power Spectrum
arxiv-2209-14220.creator: Bruno Villasenor, Brant Robertson, Piero Madau, Evan Schneider
arxiv-2209-14220.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Bruno Villasenor, Brant Robertson, Piero Madau, Evan Schneider. The forest of Lyman- α \alpha absorption lines detected in the spectra of distant quasars encodes information on the nature and properties of dark matter and the thermodynamics of diffuse baryonic material. Its main observable – the 1D flux power spectrum (FPS) – should exhibit a suppression on small scales and an enhancement on large scales in warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies compared to standard Λ \Lambda CDM.

arxiv-2212-13881.title: Mechanism of feature learning in deep fully connected networks and kernel machines that recursively learn features
arxiv-2212-13881.description: Abstract In recent years neural networks have achieved impressive results on many technological and scientific tasks. Yet, the mechanism through which these models automatically select features , or patterns in data, for prediction remains unclear. Identifying such a mechanism is key to advancing performance and interpretability of neural networks and promoting reliable adoption of these models in scientific applications.

arxiv-2311-15654.title: Event Detection in Time Series: Universal Deep Learning Approach
arxiv-2311-15654.creator: Menouar Azib, Benjamin Renard, Philippe Garnier, Vincent Génot, Nicolas André
arxiv-2311-15654.description: Abstract Event detection in time series is a challenging task due to the prevalence of imbalanced datasets, rare events, and time interval-defined events. Traditional supervised deep learning methods primarily employ binary classification, where each time step is assigned a binary label indicating the presence or absence of an event. However, these methods struggle to handle these specific scenarios effectively.

arxiv-2402-12560.title: CausalGym : Benchmarking causal interpretability methods on linguistic tasks
arxiv-2402-12560.creator: Aryaman Arora Dan Jurafsky Christopher Potts
arxiv-2402-12560.description: Abstract Language models (LMs) have proven to be powerful tools for psycholinguistic research, but most prior work has focused on purely behavioural measures (e.g., surprisal comparisons). At the same time, research in model interpretability has begun to illuminate the abstract causal mechanisms shaping LM behavior. To help bring these strands of research closer together, we introduce CausalGym .

arxiv-2410-07314.title: On the impact of AGN feedback modes onto the turbulent properties of the multiphase ICM
arxiv-2410-07314.creator: S. Sotira ,, F. Vazza and F. Brighenti
arxiv-2410-07314.description: Abstract The feedback from active galactic nuclei (AGN) plays a crucial role in regulating the thermodynamics and the dynamics of the intracluster medium (ICM). Studying the turbulent patterns of the hot and warm ionized phases may allow us to determine how these phases are involved in the AGN cycle and the amount of turbulent pressure generated by the latter.

arxiv-2501-08565.title: DualOpt: A Dual Divide-and-Optimize Algorithm for the Large-scale Traveling Salesman Problem
arxiv-2501-08565.creator: Shipei Zhou, Yuandong Ding, Chi Zhang, Zhiguang Cao, Yan Jin
arxiv-2501-08565.description: Abstract This paper proposes a dual divide-and-optimize algorithm (DualOpt) for solving the large-scale traveling salesman problem (TSP). DualOpt combines two complementary strategies to improve both solution quality and computational efficiency. The first strategy is a grid-based divide-and-conquer procedure that partitions the TSP into smaller sub-problems, solving them in parallel and iteratively refining the solution by merging nodes and partial routes.

arxiv-2509-17060.title: Going beyond Landauer: Information-cost relations from inference based on the maximum entropy principle
arxiv-2509-17060.creator: Yuanyuan Xiao, Jian-Hua Jiang, Junjie Liu
arxiv-2509-17060.description: Abstract The Landauer’s principle, a cornerstone of information thermodynamics, provides a fundamental lower bound on the energetic cost of information erasure in terms of the information content change. However, its traditional formulation is largely confined to systems exchanging solely energy with an ideal thermal bath.

arxiv-2510-20950.title: Fragmentation of Virtual Orbitals for Quantum Computing: Reducing Qubit Requirements through Many-Body Expansion
arxiv-2510-20950.creator: Federico Zahariev, Mark S. Gordon
arxiv-2510-20950.description: Abstract The development of quantum computing for molecular simulations is constrained by the limited number of qubits available on current Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices. The present work introduces the Virtual Orbital Fragmentation (FVO) method, a systematic approach that reduces qubit requirements by 40–66% while maintaining chemical accuracy.

arxiv-2602-20970.title: Spatial confinement-deconfinement transition in accelerated gluodynamics within lattice simulation
arxiv-2602-20970.creator: Viktor Braguta, Vladimir Goy, Jayanta Dey, Artem Roenko
arxiv-2602-20970.description: Abstract In this work we investigate the influence of weak acceleration on the confinement-deconfinement phase transition in gluodynamics. Our study is carried out within lattice simulation in the comoving reference frame of accelerated observer which is parameterized by the Rindler coordinates. We find that finite temperature confinement-deconfinement phase transition turns into spatial crossover in the Rindler spacetime.

pmc-10594471.title: Microbial Exudates as Biostimulants: Role in Plant Growth Promotion and Stress Mitigation
pmc-10594471.creator: Mariya Ansari, B Megala Devi, Ankita Sarkar, Anirudha Chattopadhyay, Lovkush Satnami, Pooraniammal Balu, Manoj Choudhary, Muhammad Adnan Shahid, A Abdul Kader Jailani, Ana Paula Honrado Pinto, Jorge M S Faria
pmc-10594471.description: Microbes hold immense potential, based on the fact that they are widely acknowledged for their role in mitigating the detrimental impacts of chemical fertilizers and pesticides, which were extensively employed during the Green Revolution era. The consequence of this extensive use has been the degradation of agricultural land, soil health and fertility deterioration, and a decline in crop quality.

pmc-10630681.title: Experimental investigation of usage of POE lubricants with Al2O3, graphene or CNT nanoparticles in a refrigeration compressor
pmc-10630681.creator: Kayhan Dağıdır, Kemal Bilen, Silvia Giordani
pmc-10630681.description: In this study, the use of nanolubricants containing Al2O3, graphene, and carbon nanotubes (CNTs) at different mass fractions in a refrigeration compressor was experimentally investigated. The required electrical power of the compressor was measured to determine the effect of the use of nanolubricants.

pmc-10868985.title: Discoid Lupus Erythematosus along the Lines of Blaschko in an Adult: A Case Report
pmc-10868985.creator: Aishwarya Muddebihal, Sandip Mohanty, Meenakshi Batrani
pmc-10868985.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). we present a case of 19-year-old male LDLE on the trunk. A 19-year-old male presented with asymptomatic erythematous lesions over the abdomen and trunk in a linear fashion for the past 1 year. The lesions started over the lower abdomen and progressed along the midline up to the chest and laterally at the level of left nipple in a duration of 3 months. He had no history of photosensitivity or systemic symptoms. His past, family, drug, and medical history were unremarkable.

pmc-11489826.title: A Survey on End-of-Life Contemplation Among Patients on Dialysis
pmc-11489826.creator: Martin Russwurm, Anetta Rabaev, Joachim D Hoyer, Christian S Haas, Christian Volberg, Philipp Russ
pmc-11489826.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionConsidering that mortality among patients on dialysis is high, it would be advisable for patients, relatives, and care givers to acknowledge that after dialysis initiation for many patients, the last phase in life has begun.

pmc-11505995.title: Dietary Rhythms and MASLD-Related Hepatocellular Carcinoma
pmc-11505995.creator: Nadia Malakmahmoudi, Roberta Pisu, Ezio Laconi, Fabio Marongiu, Masahito Shimizu
pmc-11505995.description: Simple SummaryDiet is a fundamental determinant of health and longevity. This relationship is complex. Historically, among the most investigated variables have been quality and quantity of food. However, over the past 2 decades increasing attention has been devoted to dietary rhythms, including time of food consumption during the day and length of fasting intervals.

pmc-11680210.title: Identification of Three Novel O-Linked Glycans in the Envelope Protein of Tick-Borne Encephalitis Virus
pmc-11680210.creator: Ebba Könighofer, Ekaterina Mirgorodskaya, Kristina Nyström, Karin Stiasny, Ambjörn Kärmander, Tomas Bergström, Rickard Nordén, Ayato Takada
pmc-11680210.description: The tick-borne encephalitis virus is a pathogen endemic to northern Europe and Asia, transmitted through bites from infected ticks. It is a member of the Flaviviridae family and possesses a positive-sense, single-stranded RNA genome encoding a polypeptide that is processed into seven non-structural and three structural proteins, including the envelope (E) protein.

pmc-12501589.title: ACTA1 gene regulation in livestock: A multidimensional review on muscle development, meat quality, and genetic applications
pmc-12501589.creator: Siti Rani Ayuti, Sangsu Shin, Eun Joong Kim, Mirni Lamid, Sunaryo Hadi Warsito, Mohammad Anam Al Arif, Widya Paramita Lokapirnasari, Zulfi Nur Amrina Rosyada, Aswin Rafif Khairullah, Muslim Akmal, Mudhita Zikkrullah Ritonga, Rimayanti Rimayanti, Mira Delima
pmc-12501589.description: The skeletal muscle α-actin gene (ACTA1) plays a pivotal role in muscle contraction, structural integrity, and overall development of skeletal muscle tissue in livestock. This review explores the complex regulatory mechanisms of ACTA1 expression and its direct impact on meat quality, animal performance, and production efficiency.

pmc-12686448.title: Pearson correlation-based clustering with collaborative task allocation in 5G Industrial Internet of Things divergent health networks
pmc-12686448.creator: Krishnakumar Vaithianathan, Julian Benadit Pernabas, Manjunath Ramanna Lamani, K. Venkatachalam, S. S. Askar, Mohamed Abouhawwash
pmc-12686448.description: Simultaneous task allocation is crucial for enhancing service quality in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) environments. The distribution and management of tasks remain among the biggest challenges in the IIoT era. Efficient allocation strategies are needed to enable transparent network configurations and maximize task throughput.

pmc-13467891.title: Evaluating the use of GLP-1 receptor agonists in Wolfram syndrome patients
pmc-13467891.creator: Laura A. Lee, Abby F. Tang, Anna E. Asako, Sarah F. Ning, Hayden A. Reed, Eleanor Duncan, Heather M. Lugar, James Hoekel, Bess A. Marshall, Tamara Hershey, Fumihiko Urano
pmc-13467891.description: IntroductionWolfram syndrome is a rare autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the WFS1 gene and characterized by early-onset, insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, optic atrophy, sensorineural hearing loss, arginine vasopressin deficiency, and progressive neurodegeneration driven by chronic endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress; no proven disease-modifying therapy currently exists.

uslaw-usc-t2-s6593.title: 2 U.S.C. § 6593 — Deputy Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper to act on death, resignation, disability, or absence of Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of Senate
uslaw-usc-t2-s6593.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t2-s6593.description: United States Code, Title 2 (The Congress); Chapter 65 (Senate Officers And Administration); Subchapter III (Sergeant At Arms And Doorkeeper Of Senate); Part A (Organization And Personnel). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In the event of the death, resignation, or disability of the Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate, the Deputy Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper shall act as Sergeant.

uslaw-usc-t6-s573.title: 6 U.S.C. § 573 — Assessments and reports
uslaw-usc-t6-s573.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t6-s573.description: United States Code, Title 6 (Domestic Security); Chapter 1 (Homeland Security Organization); Subchapter XIII (Emergency Communications). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Baseline assessment Not later than 1 year after October 4, 2006, and not less than every 5 years thereafter, the Secretary, acting through the Assistant Director for Emergency Communications, shall conduct an assessment of Federal, State, local, and tribal governments.
